title: POPANE-R4 Crossed Participant × Segment Uncertainty Sensitivity
classification: Post-primary statistical robustness sensitivity. POPANE-R1 outcomes are known.
purpose: Re-evaluate the strongest POPANE-R1 naive-persistence versus physiology contrasts with uncertainty that explicitly resamples both participants and held-out segment labels, because R1's preregistered bootstrap clustered participants only.
replication_contract: Reuse R1 file QC, anchors, targets, physiology features, horizons 1/11/21/31 s, deterministic subject folds, joint held-person × held-segment training exclusion, Ridge/HGB specifications.
Refit only the physiology-augmented model needed for the naive-vs-physiology contrast; naive prediction remains prior_affect.
Record MAE within each observed participant×segment test cell.

uncertainty.method: Crossed participant×segment bootstrap with incomplete-cell support.
uncertainty.algorithm: For each replicate independently sample the set of usable participants with replacement and the set of usable segment labels with replacement. Form the multiplicity-weighted Cartesian resample; include only participant×segment cells observed in the held-out predictions. Compute the equal-cell mean delta = MAE(naive)-MAE(physiology).
uncertainty.estimand: Equal observed participant×segment cell mean contrast. This differs from R1's participant-cluster participant-mean estimand and is explicitly a sensitivity analysis.

decisions.CROSSED_UNCERTAINTY_STRONGLY_SUPPORTS_R1: All 8 horizon×learner delta_naive_phys 95% CIs are strictly below zero.
decisions.CROSSED_UNCERTAINTY_SUPPORTS_NONPOSITIVE: No horizon×learner CI is strictly above zero, but one or more include zero.
decisions.CROSSED_UNCERTAINTY_MIXED: At least one horizon×learner CI is strictly above zero or directions materially conflict.

firewalls: Post-primary sensitivity; do not replace the frozen R1 inference.
A negative physiology increment remains predictive, not causal.
paper_role: Stress-test whether external persistence dominance survives uncertainty over both generalization axes.
